name: Discover institutional originals and retain coverage
when: An issue is researched within a declared think-tank or institutional source population.
shape: Search issue vocabulary, actors, campaigns, legal constraints and events, without requiring a target thinker or the wording of the question. Select institutions using actual publication hits plus declared registry scope and retain every selector/probe receipt. Test varied language/geographic query families within the declared scope; report effective scope and actual query/source yields. Directory membership is selection context; classification and publisher/organizer relationships require evidence. Follow original institutional pages to reports on CDNs or recordings with published transcripts, retaining the linking evidence. Shared platform hostnames alone cannot identify an institution. Keep older/undated publication leads visible separately from evidence within the requested publication window. Retain unsuccessful searches, unselected candidates and unavailable bodies; no search result cannot establish institutional silence. Seek substantive disagreement and policy proposals without manufacturing balance. Avoid counting syndication or several formats of one event as independent agreement. Analytical attribution and interpretation belong to central critical methods.
ingredients: Registry candidates and declared geography/languages/named institutions
yields: Original institutional publications and relationship evidence with measured search coverage.
misses: Unavailable originals, missing transcripts, unindexed sources and sources outside the effective language/geographic coverage; no claim of exhaustive coverage.
note: No discovery yield has yet been attributed to this practice; retain actual declared use and outcomes.
